decisions.reason: F1 omitted local path-connectedness required by the lifting criterion. Added it and proved it for simplices by convex ball intersections. The sum of all lifts commutes with faces, gives Tp*=d and p*T=sum g*, and the sign complex splits by (1-sigma*)/2, so both transfer assertions remain valid.

F4 incorrectly assigned AC to the choice-free relative CW approximation. Corrected AC to the inherited CW comparison in step 2.1 and tagged the weak-equivalence homology use in step 1.1. Qj=f transfers homology hypotheses to j, while the weak equivalence gives connectedness and simple connectedness of Z; the finite CW comparison then proves the original conclusion.

The MO normalization did not supply an R-orientation of the universal real bundle. Specified F2 coefficients and the canonical orientation from the unique nonzero fiber generator, then cited the R-oriented Thom theorem. Ordered MSO normalization retains its supplied integral orientation. Frame stabilization, disk/sphere maps, CW construction and stable colimits are unchanged; only the omitted coefficient hypothesis is supplied.

F5 incorrectly confined AC to square-algebra choices. Corrected it to include field evaluation and additive Kunneth, whose hypotheses hold since finite projective cellular homology is finite free. Cartan permits only doublings of power-of-two exponents; forced full chains and the residual admissible induction give the lexicographic leading term with coefficient one. L>=|I|+1 prevents truncation, and the d_j recover I.

Steps 1.1 and 5.1 cited an integral comparison absent from the path-loop interface. Added the published choice-free weak-equivalence integral homology theorem as the actual direct supplier. Hurewicz naturality transfers the CW generator to F; the pair LES and collapsed disk give the base generator. H_(n-1)(F)=0 for n>1 and the n=1 H0 isomorphism kill the UCT Ext terms, so both normalized evaluations are one.

F3 overstated the abutment supplied by the exact-couple interfaces. Restricted that fact to spectral-sequence construction and supplied the local convergence argument: negative filtration columns stabilize N^s=ker k, compact support exhausts boundary primitives, and the one-row E2 collapse stabilizes B^s. Exactness identifies the stable quotient with the image filtration. The local collar/layer comparison and signed orientation incidences yield the original homological Thom comparison, and finite free local cellular chains over Z give finite generation.

F3 attributed the module presentation to AC instead of the proof. Replaced it with the actual inherited AC uses and separated the Thom isomorphism in F1 from the BO(n) polynomial supplier in F2. Canonical F2 orientations license the repaired prespectrum normalization. Weight-q truncation is bijective for n>=q; unique forward/backward extension computes compatible tuples, and finite partition bounds prove degreewise finiteness.

The displayed Statement already claims pi_j(Y) tensor Q=0, so the Moore-space example does not refute it. The title omitted rational and was corrected. Also corrected F2: choice-free CW approximation is distinct from inherited AC in the rational first-Hurewicz construction. Finite induction uses A tensor Q=0 iff A is torsion to meet the next Hurewicz hypothesis; no integral homotopy vanishing is asserted.

F1 falsely inferred vanishing of an adjacent group from a single surjection or injection. Replaced it by the exact five-term chase requiring both flanking conditions. Step 1.1 already uses both correctly, including the D+1 endpoint surjection. The fiber is simply connected, rational first Hurewicz kills its homology through D, and the Serre bottom row and projection edge give the original homology comparison.

The Statement wrongly made integral Hurewicz a zero-group isomorphism above m; torsion in pi_i(S^m) need not vanish. Corrected it to the rationalized Hurewicz map, retaining the integral degree-m generator isomorphism. The strict fiber is m-connected; its rational Serre column-zero induction uses H_(b+1)(K(Z,m);Q)=0 for m<b<=2m-2. Rational homology vanishing then gives the claimed rational sphere groups. Added explicit weak-CW/integral-homology suppliers for the initial fiber vanishing.

The tautological-class definition alone does not identify w1 of a line. Added the actual projective-bundle Stiefel-Whitney definition: P(L_i)=X and x_(L_i)+w1(L_i)=0; the factor inclusion classifies L_i, giving x_(L_i)=x_i. Whitney then yields w_r(E)=P. Thom pullback and zero-section Euler pullback detect a(u_r) by the nonzero leading-monomial action a(P); componentwise inverse-limit vanishing proves injectivity.
